text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **
English philosopher THOMAS PAINE, famed for his "Give me liberty or give me death" speech, was born on this day in 1737.
United States President WILLIAM McKINLEY was born in 1843.
Australian inventor LAWRENCE HARGRAVES (the man on the 20 dollar note), was born in 1850.
American actor and comedian W.C. FIELDS, was born in 1879.

French guitarist SACHA DISTEL, who began his musical career at the age of five when he learnt to play the piano, was born in 1933. He took up the guitar at the age of 15. After hearing DIZZY GILLESPIE he became interested in modern jazz. In France he had had his biggest success with "Scoubidou" (1959) and "Mon Bon Chapeau" (1960). He made an appearance in the international charts with "Raindrops Keep Falling On My Head" (1970). SACHA recorded in five different languages and won a Grammy for the best song in 1963 with the theme song from the film "The Seven Capital Sins".."The Good Life".
American actress KATHERINE ROSS, who won an Academy Award for her performance in "THE GRADUATE", was born in 1943.

Australian pop-guru IAN "Molly" MELDRUM was born on this day in 1946. He gained a national audience when he compered "Countdown" on ABC television for 13 years. He is now a regular on the Channel 9 network's "Hey, Hey, It's Saturday".

British singer/songwriter with 'Uriah Heep' DAVID BYRON was born in 1947. From 1971 to 1978 the group had 17 hits in Germany. Their hits included "Lady In Black", "Easy Livin", "Spider Woman" and "Free Me". At the end of the seventies he was sacked from the group after disputes with the leader of the group KEN HENSLEY. He died in 1985.
American drummer from the 'Ramones' TOMMY RAMONE (TOM ERDELYI) was born in 1952. The group's music was claimed as one of the most important foundation stones of seventies punk rock.
** EVENTS **
1596 : English seaman and explorer SIR FRANCIS DRAKE was
buried at sea.
1820 : KING GEORGE III of England died at the age of 81,
after a reign of more than 59 years.
1856 : Queen VICTORIA announced the establishment of the
VICTORIA CROSS as a reward for individual bravery.
1861 : Kansas became the 34th US State.
1916 : Britain began testing military tanks.
1916 : German Zeppelins bombed Paris for the first time.
1926 : All Russian students were ordered to do military
training.
1931 : Two Australian Cabinet ministers resigned in

protest at the re-instatement of a fellow politician. EDWARD THEODORE had resigned as treasurer six months earlier over corruption allegations. He was accused of defrauding the Queensland government of 30,000 pounds in 1919, while he was premier. The two ministers JAMES FENTON and JOSEPH LYONS said THEODORE should not have returned to Cabinet before the civil proceedings against him were over. Prime Minister JAMES SCULLIN said THEODORE was needed back to deal with the financial crisis. It was believed that FENTON and LYONS were motivated by their opposition to THEODORE'S policies.
1949 : Britain recognised Israel.
1957 : The future of the Sydney Opera House was sealed

when Danish Architect JOERN UTZON's unique ideas won the design competition. The most striking feature of the design was the roof line, which was to resemble a series of gleaming white sails above the waters of the Harbour. The building that was to replace the old tram sheds at Bennelong Point was controversial from the start. Its original cost estimate was 3.5 million pounds but this figure blew out as it took from 1959 to 1973 to complete the structure. The judges of the design competition said the drawings submitted were simple to the point of being dramatic. "We are convinced that they present an opera house which is capable of being one of the great buildings of the world."
1979 : US President JIMMY CARTER commuted the prison
sentence of PATRICIA HEARST. The millionaire kidnap-victim had been sentenced to seven years' jail for joining a terrorist-group in armed robberies, but served just three years.
1980 : American comedian JIMMY DURANTE died at the age of
1987 : Soviet leader MIKHAIL GORBACHEV announced his
policy of "glasnost" (openness) to the Communist Party's Central Committee.
1987 : Phillipine President CORAZON AQUINO put down

another attempted coup against her two year-old Government. Her troops fired tear gas into the main radio and television stations in Manila which had been taken over by armed rebels. Although the coup forces had held the stations for two days they were prevented from broadcasting by loyal AQUINO officials who had cut off the electricity. Most of the rebels were said to be supporters of former President FERDINAND MARCOS.
1994 : Popular Australian author FRANK HARDY died of a
heart attack in Melbourne, at the age of 76.
